verdict.rationale: Grok Build documents a fullscreen dashboard that gives an overview of every session, showing which agents need input, which are working and which are done. Worktree sessions let parallel agents run in isolated repo copies, and /resume, /fork, subagents and background tasks round out multi-session management. Missing for 10: detail on what actions can be taken from the dashboard (switching, replying, stopping sessions) and independent or hands-on corroboration of the dashboard workflow.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can manage multiple agent-driven coding sessions from one unified workspace

citations.quote: The dashboard is a fullscreen overview of every session: which agents need input, which are working, and which are done.
A worktree session runs in an isolated copy of your repository, so parallel agents cannot overwrite each other's files.
In the TUI, `/resume` opens a picker of recent sessions for the current workspace
`/fork [directive]` branches the current session into a peer that starts from a copy of the conversation.
